note: The answers the stand-in worker gives for the demo fleet, checked by hand on 21 November 2026 against the commits in fleet.json. Each answer belongs to the advisories it names. A real agent never sees this file: it gets a copy of one app and nothing else. In each path entry, "has" is text that must be on that line; a test checks it against the fetched apps.

auth-gateway.subject: attacker
auth-gateway.why: The handler passes the token from the request body straight to JsonWebSignature.deserialize_json.

path.note: entry point POST /introspect
the token comes from the request body
direct call to the flawed function

billing-api.subject: alice
billing-api.why: The route depends on current_customer, which calls verify_bearer, which calls JsonWebSignature.deserialize. That accepts JSON serialization and hands it to the flawed function.

path.note: entry point POST /charge
the bearer token is resolved by a dependency
the dependency calls a general-purpose helper
accepts any serialization, so JSON input reaches the flawed function

session-service.why: The bearer token is verified with JsonWebToken.decode, which takes the compact format only. JSON input fails to decode before any signature check.

path.note: entry point GET /me
the only place an inbound token is checked
compact format only; the trail stops before the flawed function

token-signer.why: The service only signs, with serialize_compact. No code verifies or deserializes an inbound token.

path.note: entry point POST /sign
the only call into the library, and it signs

profile-api.why: JSON input reaches JsonWebSignature.deserialize only when the setting PROFILE_ACCEPT_JSON_TOKENS is on. It is off by default. Whether any deployment turns it on is not in the repository, so a person must decide.

path.note: entry point GET /profile
JSON tokens are refused here unless the setting is on
with the setting on, JSON input reaches the flawed function
the setting, off by default

link-redirector.why: The route /legacy/(.*) is a RedirectHandler whose target is "/{0}", so the path the caller sends starts the redirect target. A path with three slashes redirects to another host.

path.note: the application and its route table
RedirectHandler: the captured path starts the target

docs-portal.why: RedirectHandler is used four times, always with a fixed target or with a target that has the fixed prefix /manual/ in front of the captured path. No capture group starts a target, so no request can redirect to another host.

path.note: fixed target
the captured path follows the fixed prefix /manual/
fixed target
fixed target; the trail stops here

html-extractor.why: The caller's selector string goes to Beautiful Soup's select(), which hands it to the Soup Sieve selector parser. Only a selector syntax error is caught.

path.note: entry point POST /extract
the selector comes from the request body
Beautiful Soup passes the selector to the flawed parser

link-checker.why: Every selector passed to select() and select_one() is a constant in the code. The caller controls the HTML only, and the flaw is in parsing the selector.

path.note: entry point POST /links: the request holds html and base_url only
the selectors are module constants (lines 11 to 15)
a constant selector; the trail stops before caller input reaches a selector

ticket-mailer.why: requirements.txt pins mail-parser, but no file imports it. The service only writes mail, with the standard library's EmailMessage.

path.note: the package is pinned here
entry point POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/notify
mail is written with the standard library; nothing imports mailparser
